scope: PrintSim-focused source/design review only; direct target-aware timestep builder, not a call! adapter or arbitrary-call capture promise
answer: Direct target-aware timestep construction, standard device-array sum! outputs and explicit configuration/diagnostic contracts now have a coherent target shape; the actual Group/shared-operation port and native qualification are not implemented.
mantle_responsibilities: One shared eager/recorded operation definition and capability selector
Explicit Group/repeat/when control and raw kernel emission
Device-owned resource uses, scratch placement, ordering, derived-workspace retirement and recorded snapshots
proposed_user_code:
frame = Graph(dev)
physics = Group(frame, "physics")
PrintSim.step!(physics, world, state, dt)
repeat!(physics, substeps)
# Add rendering nodes using the SAME device-owned state arrays.
run!(frame)
proposal_limit: Use the existing explicit-target graph-building interface directly, generalized to Group. The builder composes call! array operations/raw dispatches during construction; it needs no call! wrapper, operation registration or CPU execution during replay. No new Mantle Solver class or per-backend solver implementation is proposed.
operator_seam: Standard mul! for assembled or matrix-free operators, through call! when recorded
Standard ldiv! for preconditioner application, through call! when recorded
Standard sum!(f,r,A) uses an ordinary one-element device array r, returned identically; convergence kernels read r[1]. Existing world_dot! device-output kernels remain valid.
remaining_design_questions: Implement and qualify operator/reduction definitions using the documented shared recipe boundary; retain valid existing target-aware kernels.
Apply sparse/matrix-free/preconditioner schema and invalidation contracts to actual FEM/AScanner migration.
Keep dt-dependent setup recompute/rebuild/reject and diagnostic host-boundary rules explicit in the actual port.

source_constraints.fact: Existing helper is explicitly target-aware, rejects diagnostic callbacks while recording, converts dt to Float32 and rejects a timestep different from the constructed FEM solver.
Coarse rest matrix is factored on the host once for the configured timestep; runtime restrictions/triangular solves/prolongations are device work.
Current diagnostics/controller modes use reusable phase graphs; a pure GPU loop and per-iteration CPU callbacks are not the same execution contract.
Graph-only recording classification and launch methods need portable Group support; wrapping/adapting arrays is not the fix.

parameter_rule: Updating a GPURef cannot by itself refresh a timestep-dependent operator or coarse factor. The PrintSim definition must recompute/rebuild affected setup or explicitly reject such changes; preserve persistent simulation state as appropriate.
diagnostic_rule: Keep a GPU-only resident mode. CPU diagnostics require explicit host boundaries/controller orchestration and measured synchronization; do not hide callbacks inside a supposedly baked GPU-controlled loop.
correction: The earlier call!(physics, PrintSim.step!, ...) proposal put a target-aware graph builder at the wrong layer. Ordinary supported array operations use call! inside the builder; the timestep builder itself is called directly.
